{{Short description|Theorem in complex analysis}}

'''Pólya's shire theorem''', named after [[George Pólya]], is a theorem in [[complex analysis]] that describes the asymptotic distribution of the zeros of successive derivatives of a [[meromorphic function]] on the complex plane.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pólya |first=George |date=1922 |title=Über die Nullstellen sukzessiver Derivierten |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01482068 |journal=[[Math. Zeit.]] |volume=12 |pages=36–60|doi=10.1007/BF01482068 }}</ref> It has applications in [[Nevanlinna theory]].<ref name=Hayman>{{cite book |last=Hayman |first=W. |author-link=Walter Hayman |title=Meromorphic Functions |chapter=Distribution of the values of meromorphic functions and their derivatives |pages=55–78 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |year=1964 |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/meromorphicfunct0000haym/page/62/mode/2up}}</ref>{{rp|pp=55,62}}

== Statement ==
Let <math>f</math> be a meromorphic function on the complex plane with <math>P \neq \emptyset</math> as its set of poles. If <math>E</math> is the set of all zeros of all the successive derivatives <math>f', f'', f^{(3)}, \ldots</math>, then the [[Derived set (mathematics)|derived set]] <math>E'</math> (or the set of all limit points) is as follows:

# if <math>f</math> has only one pole, then <math>E' </math> is empty.
# if <math>|P| \geq 2</math>, then <math>E'</math> coincides with the edges of the [[Voronoi diagram]] determined by the set of poles <math>P</math>. In this case, if <math>a \in P</math>, the interior of each Voronoi cell consisting of the points closest to <math>a</math> than any other point in <math>P</math> is called the <math>a</math>-''shire''.<ref name=Whittaker>{{Cite book |last=Whittaker |first=J.M. |author-link=John Macnaghten Whittaker |title=Interpolatory Function Theory |date=1935 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |pages=32–38 |url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.77626/page/n41/mode/2up}}</ref>

The derived set is independent of the order of each pole.<ref name=Whittaker/>{{rp|p=32}}

In the special case of a rational function <math>f</math> with at least two distinct poles, the theorem has a measure-theoretic refinement: the normalized zero-counting measures of <math>f^{(n)}</math> converge to an explicitly described probability measure supported on the edges of the Voronoi diagram of the poles.<ref name=BogvadHagg>{{cite journal |last1=Bøgvad |first1=Rikard |last2=Hägg |first2=Christian |date=2017 |title=A refinement for rational functions of Pólya's method to construct Voronoi diagrams |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X17302329 |journal=[[Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications]] |volume=452 |issue=1 |pages=312–334 |doi=10.1016/j.jmaa.2017.02.071 |arxiv=1610.00921}}</ref>
